status: Experiment hypotheses for round 3, derived from rtl-2.1 after the heldout-1 verdict; not approved product settings. Lookup fields (H1-H7) are unchanged, so lookup output differs from rtl-2.1 only in policy_id/policy_sha256. Block changes: H11 phrase variants limited to singular/plural (block_phrase_morphology_number_only), and H13 paired queries (block_query_design = paired_append) replace the H9 suggested-query composition. Decided on development data (dev repositories and the consumed heldout-1 cases) before any heldout-2 run.
lemma_fallback_rule: H5: when neither the exact key nor the token key matches a dictionary expression, strip one regular inflection from the last word of the exact key and use the first resulting key that exists as a dictionary exact key (match_kind = lemma_fallback). Rule order: -s (not after s), -es, -ies -> -y, then -ing and -ed, each tried with e-restoration first (pars -> parse, which also covers -d), then bare, then with a doubled final consonant undoubled (runn -> run). Bases shorter than 3 letters are not tried. Candidates identical to the lemma's token key or index tokens are rejected as same_as_query.
repository_presence: H1 (changed for phrases): a single-index-token candidate is kept when its token has file_count >= 1, as in rtl-1. A multi-token candidate is kept only when its index tokens concatenated without a separator (event loop -> eventloop) have file_count >= 1 (phrase_evidence = concatenated), or when one of its non-excluded relation kinds is listed in phrase_evidence_relation_kinds and every component has file_count >= 1 (phrase_evidence = components_only). Otherwise it is rejected with reason phrase_without_identifier_evidence; the presence field still records component presence.
commonness_rule: H2: drop a single-index-token candidate whose live-file fraction exceeds the value. Multi-token candidates have no defined fraction and are not filtered. The value is a hypothesis; per-candidate counts are saved so other cutoffs can be recomputed without rerunning.
final_limit_rule: H3: at most this many final terms per input after deduplication; every earlier-stage candidate stays in the output. Morphology words never count toward this limit.
ordering: H4 (changed): relation-kind priority, then the query word's WordNet sense order (0 = most frequent; non-WordNet evidence = 0), then repository file count descending (single token: its count; multi-token: the concatenated identifier's count when present, else the smallest component count), then more supporting relations, then exact_key.
deduplication: Candidates with identical index-token sequences (for example 'publish-subscribe' and 'publish subscribe') collapse to the first in order.
not_ready_behavior: When repository statistics are not ready (stale, missing, incompatible, unavailable, not configured), no final terms are produced; dictionary candidates are still reported as not_evaluated, and morphology reports repository_not_ready with no words.
morphology_rule: H6: for a query with exactly one index token (ASCII letters, length >= 3), return published repository words that share the query's Snowball English stem (tantivy Stemmer, read from the index-time word_stems table), excluding the query itself, in a separate morphology list that is never mixed into dictionary candidates, final_terms, or final_limit. A word is typed inflection when, under the H5 suffix rules, it is an inflection base of the query, the query is its base, or both share a base (sibling inflections such as executing/executed); otherwise derivation. The list is ordered by file count descending (then word) and capped at morphology_limit. query_file_count and query_absent_in_repository are reported for every query.
morphology_prefix_rule: H7: prefix family typed same_root. (a) When the query starts with a listed prefix and the remainder has at least morphology_min_prefix_remainder_length letters, add published words sharing the remainder's stem (reconnect -> connect, connection). (b) For the query and each of its same-stem words, add prefix + word when that exact word has a word_stems row (lock, locked -> unlock, unlocked); this uses point lookups only, never a vocabulary scan. String prefixes are not morphemes: false families such as display/play are expected and measured, not filtered.
block_rule: H8 (changed for phrases): rtpoc2 block expands each input term that is not identifier-shaped (codemap-search split_identifier yields more than one token, or the term contains '::' or '.'); identifier-shaped terms pass through with reason identifier_shaped and are never expanded or replaced. Dictionary lookup always runs on the whole term (exact, token_normalized, then H5 lemma fallback) and lists up to block_dictionary_terms_per_term final dictionary terms (relation kind plus the gloss of the first non-excluded evidence that has one, trimmed to block_gloss_max_chars); each dictionary term replaces the whole term. Morphology follows H11 and is capped at block_morphology_words_per_term per term. --mode selects dictionary, morphology, both, or control_terms_only (H12). The task query is recorded only. Each term records shown_expansions: how many of its expansions block_text shows after the H10 byte cap, in rendered order.
block_morphology_types_reason: Development labels (v2-run-1, codex gpt-6.1-sol, v1 rubric; .codemap/poc/related-terms/evaluation/development-v2/v2-run-1/reports/fresh-labels-v2/comparison.json): inflection 98/110 useful or form variant, derivation 9/20, same_root 6/35 (mostly related_only such as deserialize->serialize, replace->place). Decided on development data before any held-out run.
block_phrase_morphology_number_only_reas: Development labels of the consumed heldout-1 run (now development data; codex gpt-6.1-sol, feature precision rubric): phrase variants that change only singular/plural were 87-100% useful, while phrase -ed/-ing variants were 25-66% (index version -> indexed version). Single-token terms keep every inflection (69-99%). Estimated shown-term precision with this rule: 91.0% (479 labeled pairs).
phrase_morphology_rule: H11 (new): a term with one index token runs H6/H7 morphology on the whole term (any stemmable length, no stopword filter) and each variant's replacement is the variant itself. A non-identifier term with several index tokens runs H6/H7 morphology (same function) on each distinct index token whose length is at least block_phrase_morphology_min_token_length and that is not in block_phrase_morphology_stopwords; other tokens are recorded with handling too_short or stopword. Each variant records its token and a replacement: the phrase's lowercase index tokens joined by single spaces with every occurrence of that token replaced by the variant (file watcher -> file watchers). The block reads each token's whole stem family (morphology_limit caps only the lookup output), keeps only variants whose type is listed in block_morphology_types, and then orders and caps them, so the type filter never runs on an already truncated list. Inside a term, variants are ordered by: variants of tokens absent from the repository (token file_count = 0) first, then type inflection -> derivation -> same_root, then variants of the rarer token (token file_count ascending), then variant file_count descending, then token position and word; the first block_morphology_words_per_term are kept. The same order applies to single-token terms. The minimum length removes short tokens whose Snowball families are mostly noise (id, ip, ui); the stopword list holds English function words of length >= 4 (shorter ones are already removed by the length rule). Neither value is tuned. rtl-2.2: when block_phrase_morphology_number_only is true, a phrase token keeps only variants that are its regular English singular or plural (-es only after s, x, z, ch, sh; consonant + y -> -ies; -s otherwise); single-token terms are not affected.
block_query_max_words_reason: Changed from 3: held-out agent terms are mostly one- or two-word phrases (terms-feature-test.json: 42% one word, 54% two words, 4% three words), so a phrase replacement (2 words) plus one phrase anchor (2 words) needs 4 words; with 3, phrase replacements could take only single-word anchors.
suggested_query_rule: Superseded in rtl-2.2 by H13 (paired_query_rule) for the dictionary, morphology, and both modes; kept for reference. H9 (changed): expanded terms whose query is absent in the repository come first, then input order. Each term's replacements are taken in order (absent in repository: morphology then dictionary; otherwise dictionary then morphology) and each is combined with up to block_anchor_words_max anchors: the other input terms (identifier-shaped ones included) with the smallest positive repository file count (single token: its count; phrase: the concatenated identifier's count when present, else the smallest component count; ties by input order). An anchor whose words would exceed block_query_max_words is replaced by its rarest single index token (smallest positive file count, earliest on ties) when that token fits; an anchor (or fallback token) repeating a query word is skipped. Queries without an anchor or below block_query_min_words are skipped; duplicates by lowercase word set are dropped; generation stops at block_suggested_query_limit.
control_query_rule: In rtl-2.2 the H12 list below is emitted only by --mode control_terms_only; the dictionary, morphology, and both modes emit the H13 paired control queries. H12 (new): control_queries contain input terms only and are emitted in every mode; --mode control_terms_only also uses them as suggested_queries and lists no expansions. Each expanded term (H9 term order) has control candidates in this order: the H9 query with the term itself as the only replacement, the term combined with each single H9 anchor (anchor order, same composition limits), then the term alone when it has between block_query_min_words and block_query_max_words words. Candidates are taken round-robin across terms (every term's first candidate, then every term's second, ...), deduplicated by lowercase word set, up to block_suggested_query_limit. The first control query of each term equals the rtl-2.1 round-0 control. An evaluation that issues k suggested queries compares against the first k control queries (fewer only when the input terms allow no more).
block_size_rule: H10: block_text never exceeds max_block_bytes. Lowest-ranked expansions are dropped first (latest rank position, later term on ties), then suggested queries from the end, then term lines from the end, and only then are bytes cut at a character boundary. Every omission is counted in block_omissions.
paired_query_rule: H13 (new, rtl-2.2): suggested and control queries come in pairs. Only expanded terms that have at least one related term in the mode take part, in H9 term order. Each such term's H12 control candidates (term with its H9 anchors, term with each single anchor, term alone) are used round-robin across terms; for each control query the suggested query is the same control query with the term's next usable related term appended (related terms are tried in turn; one is usable when it adds a new word and repeats no earlier suggestion) (a morphology variant appends only its variant word, e.g. org users + user; a dictionary term appends the whole term). A control query is skipped when it repeats an earlier control word set or none of its term's related terms is usable. At most block_suggested_query_limit pairs. control_queries lists the paired control queries in the same order, so a treatment set differs from its control set only by the appended related terms. Suggested queries may exceed block_query_max_words by the appended term.
paired_query_reason: heldout-1 (now development data) showed that H9 spent all five suggested queries on the first one or two terms (mean 2.5 of 5.75 expandable terms varied) while the control spread over five terms, so allocation, not related terms, decided the comparison (control recovered 4 of 9 baseline misses, treatment 3). With paired_append on the same data: treatment 3, control 4, recovered beyond control 0; the pairing removes the allocation difference so that any recovery beyond control is caused by the related terms.
